subject: tigerfish
title: This Fish Leaps Out of a Lake and Catches Swallows in Mid-Air

scenes.text: Swallows skim this African lake to drink. Some never fly back up.
The hunter isn't a hawk or a crocodile. It's waiting underwater.
At Schroda Dam in South Africa, scientists filmed tigerfish leaping up to a meter out of the water.
Some chase a swallow along the surface. Others rocket up from deep water, and that works better.
In fifteen days, the fish caught around three hundred swallows. Up to twenty a day.
People had told stories of bird-eating fish for decades. Now it's on camera.

description:
African tigerfish at Schroda Dam in South Africa's Mapungubwe National Park were filmed leaping out of the water to catch barn swallows in flight, the first documented case (Journal of Fish Biology, 2014).
They used two tactics: chasing along the surface, or a direct strike from deeper water. About 300 swallows were taken over the 15-day survey, up to 20 a day.
Which animal surprise would you want to see filmed next?
thumbnail_text: FISH CATCHES BIRDS IN THE AIR
first_comment: The deep-water strike worked better than the surface chase. Would you believe this if you hadn't seen it filmed?
